title: Daily Temperatures
statement:
Given an array `temperatures` of daily temperatures, return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the number of days you have to wait after day `i` to get a warmer temperature.

If no warmer day ever comes, `answer[i]` is `0`.

steps.caption: Keep the days still waiting for a warmer one.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 73, so day 0 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Day 1 is 74, warmer than day 0's 73. That is the first warmer day for 0, so it waited 1 day(s) and stops waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 74, so day 1 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Day 2 is 75, warmer than day 1's 74. That is the first warmer day for 1, so it waited 1 day(s) and stops waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 75, so day 2 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 71, so day 3 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 69, so day 4 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Day 5 is 72, warmer than day 4's 69. That is the first warmer day for 4, so it waited 1 day(s) and stops waiting.
Day 5 is 72, warmer than day 3's 71. That is the first warmer day for 3, so it waited 2 day(s) and stops waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 72, so day 5 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Day 6 is 76, warmer than day 5's 72. That is the first warmer day for 5, so it waited 1 day(s) and stops waiting.
Day 6 is 76, warmer than day 2's 75. That is the first warmer day for 2, so it waited 4 day(s) and stops waiting.
Nothing left on the stack is cooler than 76, so day 6 joins the queue of days still waiting.
Whatever is still waiting never warmed up, so those stay 0. Answer: [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0].

checkpoints.question: Days 2, 3 and 4 are all waiting. When a warmer day finally arrives, which one does it answer first?
options: day 2, which has been waiting longest
all three at once, since one warm day settles them together
checkpoints.why: The waiting days get cooler as you go right, so the newest is the easiest to beat. A day warm enough for an older one must pass the newer ones first.

checkpoints.question: Day 6 is 76 and has just settled day 5. Does it stop there?
options: no — it keeps settling while the top is still cooler
yes — each day answers at most one waiting day
yes — the rest have to wait for a day warmer than 76
checkpoints.answer: no — it keeps settling while the top is still cooler
checkpoints.why: One warm day can end several waits at once. Stopping after one is the common bug: day 2 has been waiting since the start and 76 answers it too.

hints: Comparing every day against every later day works, but re-reads the same stretch over and over. What do you already know about the days you have passed and not yet answered?
A day is still waiting only until something warmer shows up. When today is warmer than a waiting day, today is that day's answer — and today can settle several waiting days at once, newest first.

Walk forward keeping the indices of days whose answer is still unknown. Before adding today, keep taking the most recent waiting day for as long as today is warmer than it, recording the gap between them each time. Then today joins the waiting list. Anything still unanswered at the end never warmed up.
